commonErrors.why: You calculated f(2) = 2⁵ = 32, which is the value of the function, not its derivative.
You decreased the exponent and forgot to subtract it by a factor. 2⁴ = 16, then you must multiply by 5.
You lowered the power and multiplied it by x without raising it to the new power : 5 × 2 = 10.
You multiply the two derivatives: 2x × 1 = 4 by x = 2. The product rule is the sum of two terms, not the product of two derivatives. The counterexample in the derivation above shows why.
You calculated f(2) = 5 × (−1) = −5, which is the value of the function, not its derivative.
You made a mistake in the sign inside 2x(x − 3) and added 12 instead of subtracting it.

You reversed the order of subtraction in the numerator and wrote f g′ − f′ g. The correct order begins with the derivative of the numerator multiplied by the denominator, and subtraction is not commutative.
You did not square the denominator, so you divided by (3 − 1) = 2 instead of 4.
You calculated f(3) = 4/2 = 2, which is the value of the function, not its derivative.

questions.solution: ‎f′ = 4(2x + 5)³ × 2 = 8(2x + 5)³‎. When x = −2 is 2x + 5 = 1, the result is 8 × 1 = 8.

commonErrors.why: You neglected the inner derivative. 4(1)³ = 4, and it is correct to multiply it by g′ = 2. This factor is the whole difference between the power rule and the chain rule.
You calculated f(−2) = 1⁴ = 1, which is the value of the function, not its derivative.
You multiplied by 2 twice, or used the exponent 4 without reducing it to 3.

questions.solution: Rewrite: f(x) = 3x⁻². So f′ = 3(−2)x⁻³ = −6x⁻³ = −6/x³, and at x = 1 it equals −6.

commonErrors.why: You neglected the negative sign resulting from lowering the exponent −2. The function 3/x² is decreasing at x = 1, so its derivative is inevitably negative.
You calculated f(1) = 3, which is the value of the function, not its derivative.
You neglected the parameter 3 and derived x⁻² alone.
I forgot the derivative of the internal function 3x.
Derivation of the equation gives the subtraction of the term 2x when isolated.
Forgot the inside derivative 2x.
The value of the first derivative is quartered instead of differentiating it.
I used the derivative of a constant instead of tracking the variable exponent and base.
